summary: Dire Bear Form the whole fight: Mangle (Bear) on cooldown (top threat), Lacerate to build and hold a 5-stack bleed, Maul as the off-GCD rage dump, Swipe for AoE. Maintain Faerie Fire (Feral) and Demoralizing Roar. Bears have no block/parry - mitigation is passive armor + dodge, so there's no per-GCD defensive cast.
_dev_note: Wrong-expansion guard (do NOT surface to users): Survival Instincts and Berserk are WotLK abilities; kept in off_rotation for detection but user-facing notes stay terse.

breakpoint.note: Mangle (Bear) cast count should be near its theoretical max (used on its ~6s cooldown) - it's the top single-target threat and the #1 bear competence signal. Lacerate should ramp to and hold a 5-stack bleed. Maul (off the GCD) should appear frequently as the rage dump, riding alongside Mangle/Lacerate; no Maul means rage capping and wasted threat.

advisory: TBC bear tank. Should be in Dire Bear Form the entire fight - any Cat-form abilities (Shred, Rip, Rake, Mangle Cat) mean the druid is in Cat (DPS), not tanking. Bears have no Shield Block/Holy Shield equivalent; mitigation is passive (high armor + dodge), so don't expect a per-GCD defensive cast. Frenzied Regeneration is a cooldown-style self-heal on damage spikes (a handful per fight), not a rotational ability. Barkskin and Challenging Roar (AoE taunt) are situational cooldowns. Fight notes: bears are the premier AoE-threat tank in TBC - on add-heavy pulls (Hyjal trash waves, Mount Hyjal/SSC packs, Karathress totems) tab-Swipe with Demoralizing Roar and ride Maul for extra cleave threat; on single-target bosses, Mangle (Bear) on cooldown plus a held 5-stack Lacerate carries threat, and save Barkskin/Frenzied Regeneration for predictable spike windows.
